text.tspan: Path MTU discovery: a too-big packet with DF set, and the ICMP that fixes it
h1
r1
r2
h2
① h1 sends 1500 bytes with DF (Don't Fragment) set
ping -M do -s 1472: 1472 data + 8 ICMP + 20 IP
r1: 1500 > next link's 1400 and DF is set
→ drop it (can't fragment) and tell the sender
② r1 → h1: ICMP type 3 code 4 · From 10.0.1.1 icmp_seq=1 Frag needed and DF set (mtu = 1400)
③ h1 caches path MTU 1400 for this destination
next 1500-byte try: local error: message too long, mtu=1400
④ h1 sends 1400 bytes (1372 + 28): fits
PMTUD black hole: a firewall drops the ICMP in ②
h1 never learns and keeps sending 1500-byte packets, which vanish. TCP handshake and small requests work,
large responses hang (Lab 3.5 fault 8: headers, then 0 bytes, then a timeout)
Fixes (both verified in Lab 3.5)
Fix 1: allow ICMP type 3 code 4 (ICMPv6: type 2).
Never block all ICMP.
Fix 2: clamp the TCP MSS on the router:
iptables … -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
Where it bites
VPNs and tunnels: extra headers
VXLAN overlays in Kubernetes: MTU 1450 inside
AWS: MTU 9001 inside a VPC, but 1500 across the
internet, VPN and some peering paths
MTU 1500
MTU 1400
unchanged
